page_title: Honeycomb’s O’Reilly Book Observability Engineering, 2nd Ed.

summary.name: Observability Engineering, 2nd Edition
summary.one_liner: A 2nd edition O'Reilly book by Charity Majors, Liz Fong-Jones, George Miranda, and Austin Parker on applying observability in software teams, including AI-era instrumentation and governance.
use_cases: learning how to apply observability in an engineering organization
instrumenting AI agents and nondeterministic workloads in production
drafting SLOs shared by business and engineering teams
governance decisions on observability for CTOs and engineering leaders
finding production faults faster with telemetry
summary.what_it_does: The page promotes the second edition of Observability Engineering, which the publisher says is almost entirely rewritten and twice as long, with 27 new chapters. It covers an introduction to observability, building and understanding code with observability with and without AI, and a new section on observability governance for technical decision-makers. Topics listed include instrumenting AI agents, collaborative SLO drafting, connecting code to customer impact, and faster fixes using data-rich analytics. The page also advertises an on-demand observability masterclass by Liz Fong-Jones and lists guest contributors.
notable: Second edition almost entirely rewritten, with 27 net-new chapters
Includes a new observability governance section for CTOs, VPs, and staff+ engineers
Covers instrumentation for AI agents and nondeterministic workloads
Companion on-demand observability masterclass by Liz Fong-Jones
caveats: Page is a book promotion; purchase price and formats are not stated on the page
Content is oriented to observability practice and Honeycomb's perspective
